chunks: Dawud ibn Sirhan asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
About a guarantor and a pledge in a deferred sale,
He said: "There is no harm in it."

key_terms.الرَّهْنِ: a pledged asset held as security for a debt
key_terms.النَّسِيئَةِ: deferred payment sale; a sale on credit
key_terms.الْكَفِيلِ: a guarantor who undertakes responsibility for the obligation
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to require a guarantor or collateral in a deferred sale in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states that taking a guarantor or a pledge in a deferred sale is permissible. It indicates the validity of using financial security measures in credit-based transactions within Islamic legal practice.
